To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

nonequilibrium solid solutions with a positive deviation of lattice parameter from Vegard’s law and a high level of hardness are formed during severe plastic deformation of Cu–Ag powders under pressure.

the mechanical alloying (MA) of Cu1− xAg x powders with the deformation under pressure leads to the formation of nonequilibrium solid solutions with the FCC structure, the chemical homogeneity of which is confirmed by the results of electron probe microanalysis and X-ray diffraction.

the mechanical alloying (MA) of the Cu1.0 – xAgx powders with deformation under pressure leads to the formation of a nonequilibrium nanocrystal FCC solid solutions with a high degree of chemical and structural homogeneity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the formation of nonequilibrium solid solutions of copper with silver upon severe deformation under a pressure of 5 GPa and the investigation of their structure and properties.
the synthesis, properties and decomposition of nonequilibium solid solution alloys of copper and silver obtained by mechanical alloying and deformation under pressure.
the formation of nonequilibrium solid solutions in Cu–Ag systems under severe plastic deformation and their properties.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the formation of nonequilibrium solid solutions of Cu1. 0 − x-Ag x (x = 1.0, 1.1, …, 1.9) upon severe deformation under high pressure and the properties of the alloys are determined by the formation and evolution of a disperse structure and the formation of a solid solution.

nonequilibrium solid solutions with the FCC structure are obtained upon the mechanical alloying under pressure of copper and silver with a high degree of homogeneity, which is retained after the thermal decomposition of the solid solutions.
the formation of nonequilibrium Cu-Ag alloys by mechanical alloying is a very effective and promising method for obtaining nanocrystallized alloys with unique properties.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the formation of nonequilibrium nanocrystals in the Cu-Ag system is possible under severe plastic deformation of powders with the formation of a solid solution.
the formation of nonequilibrium FCC solid solutions with a high degree of chemical homogeneity and high mechanical properties is possible by the mechanical alloying under pressure.

the formation of nonequilibrium nanocrystals with the FCC lattice upon severe deformation under high pressure and the properties of such materials are determined by the chemical composition and the degree of nonequilibrium of the initial powders.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to form nonequilibrium solid solutions with a nanosize crystallite size by the severe deformation of powders under pressure.
it is possible to form nonequilibrium solid solutions with a high degree of chemical homogeneity by mechanical alloying and deformation under pressure.

the mechanical alloying under pressure can be used to obtain nonequilibrium nanocrystaline solid solutions with the FCC structure and the positive deviation of the lattice parameter from the Vegard rule.
